<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
        <jats:p>As autonomous systems become more embedded into our environments, the ability of these systems to anticipate the future actions of humans will become invaluable for providing assistance and safety measures. Egocentric action anticipation is a task in which a future activity must be predicted using first-person footage. This project is a survey that aims to provide an updated view of advancements within this task, to guide architecture design for future implementations. This survey has chosen a range of publicly available egocentric action anticipation models. An analysis of the models revealed that this task's predictive architectures tend to fall into either a recurrent network or a transformer. The evaluation of the models on two datasets revealed that the transformer-based "Adaptive Video Transformer' and `Temporal Aggregation' generally outperformed all the recursive architectures in this survey. These results demonstrate that the attention-based architecture of the transformer is valuable within vision prediction tasks and that future design of predictive architecture should focus on using attention-based models.</jats:p>
title: Deep-learning Based Egocentric Action Anticipation: A Survey
